item.title: Why should only the surgeon have a 3D view of the operation?
item.dc:creator: XREAL_Global
item.content:encoded:
Why should only the surgeon have a 3D view of the operation?
At Vanderbilt University Medical Center, head and neck cancer surgeon Dr. Michael Topf is using XREAL AURA and apoQlar's HoloMedicine® platform to bring stereoscopic surgical views to more members of the operating room team.
With HoloMedicine Robotics, additional team members can see the surgeon's perspective. And with Shared Experience, surgeons, radiologists, oncologists and pathologists can explore the same 3D medical model together, in real time.
From surgical collaboration to medical education, spatial computing is changing how medical teams visualize, share and understand complex anatomy.
#XREAL #AURA #AndroidXR
Android XR is a trademark of Google LLC. https://x.com/XREAL_Global/status/2118706620293120077/video/1

item.title: Thanks for following along!
item.dc:creator: RokidGlobal
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for following along! We can’t wait to show you more at CES 2027.👓✨ https://x.com/milhouscc/status/2115830475377840239
引用 @milhouscc：Are we getting an iPhone moment for AI glasses here?
Too early to tell, but damn... Rokid Color has me excited about this category again.
Rokid just unveiled Color at its launch event in Hangzhou, China. Seeing that name light up the stage makes the ambition pretty clear: a richer visual interface, right in front of your eyes.
Full color opens up interesting possibilities. A photo you can actually assess before taking it. A map where different routes are easier to distinguish. Visual context that could make an AI answer quicker to understand than another spoken paragraph.
Those are the kinds of experiences that make me curious. But a great screen is only one part of a product people will want to wear.
For me, the harder questions are about the ordinary moments between the demos.
Can I keep the glasses on for hours without thinking about the weight, heat, or battery? Can I interact discreetly when talking out loud would be awkward? Can the AI show me something useful at the right moment, then get out of the way?
And can it do that reliably enough that reaching for my phone starts to feel like the slower option?
That's where the engineering gets interesting. More visual capability creates more choices about what to show, when to show it, and what deserves the user's attention. Putting a phone-sized pile of notifications into someone's field of view would be a pretty disappointing use of it.
I'd much rather have a few things that work beautifully: a clear direction at a confusing junction, help understanding something in front of me, or a quick action that doesn't turn into a conversation with a chatbot. Those are possibilities I'm excited about, not claims that Color has already nailed them.
An unveiling can't establish an iPhone moment. That takes a product people keep choosing after the novelty wears off.
Rokid Color has my attention because it makes that future easier to picture. Earning a place in everyday life is what would make it matter.
#RokidColor
https://m.sohu.com/a/1093852339_549351 https://x.com/milhouscc/status/2115830475377840239/photo/1

item.title: Life doesn’t stop at the edge of a virtual screen.
item.dc:creator: XREAL_Global
item.content:encoded: Life doesn’t stop at the edge of a virtual screen. Read a verification code on your phone. Check a handwritten note. Look up to talk with someone beside you. XREAL AURA’s optical see-through lenses let you see your surroundings directly. Video passthrough headsets show a camera-captured view instead. How much fine detail does each viewing path preserve? We built on our longstanding collaboration with TÜV Rheinland, a global testing and certification organization with more than 150 years of experience. In TÜV Rheinland’s simulated indoor bench test, AURA, using OST technology, retained 92.0% of the reference fine-pattern contrast at 10 cycles per degree, compared with 19.6% for the traditional VST headset used in the test. Your digital space. A direct connection to the world around you. #XREAL #AURA #AndroidXR #TUVRheinland *Relative to an unobstructed reference. Results describe the tested devices and laboratory setup, not overall image quality or reading performance. Normal-wear equivalence of the VST setup has not been established. Test report ID: CN26Z2PP 001. https://x.com/XREAL_Global/status/2115897128971042888/photo/1

item.content:encoded: We went to see how Tesla builds cars. Our glasses came along to document it. 👓⚡ Much of the POV footage in this video was recorded on Rokid Glasses during our visit to Tesla’s Gigafactory in Austin. Wearing the camera gave us a way to share the tour as we experienced it, with our hands free to do something other than hold a phone. Outside the factory, members of the Tesla community got to try Rokid Glasses themselves. We’re usually the ones answering questions about our tech, so it was fun to spend a day being curious about someone else’s, too.
